issue.title: Browse.vc.db is not invalidated in vs2019 when VcpkgTriplet changes

repository.name: vcpkg
repository.description: C++ Library Manager for Windows, Linux, and MacOS

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Ignoring the recent break I reported (https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/issues/12062), when you set VcpkgTriplet in a vcxproj file, VS2015 and VS2017 consistently look in the correct location for the header files from the installed vcpkg ports. But in VS2019, while the compile behaves appropriately, when you try to open a header file from a port, it can look in the wrong location if you've changed the triplet. This is a bug and poor integration experience that seems to works correctly in VS2015 and VS2017.

**Environment**
- OS: Win 1903, 1909
- Compiler: Bad behavior in VS2019 16.6.2

**To Reproduce**
- Install `vcpkg` without the recent `.vcxproj` triplet bug, and install `minhook:x86-windows-static` (just to have something to use):
```
git clone https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg.git vcpkg_before
cd vcpkg_before
git checkout 14514508d8d30bdbd645b2bec89696aec25497f1~1
.\bootstrap-vcpkg.bat
.\vcpkg.exe integrate install
.\vcpkg.exe install minhook:x86-windows-static
```
- Now start visual studio 2019 (16.6.2), create a new c++ console application project with solution.
Add
`#include "minhook.h"`
immediately before the main() function.
- Build the solution. It will correctly fail as only the static minhook is installed.
- Right click on the text "minhook.h" in the text of the include line you added. Choose to go to document. This correctly fails.
- Close visual studio.
- Edit the `.vcxproj` project file to have the line:
`<VcpkgTriplet>x86-windows-static</VcpkgTriplet>`
at the bottom of the
`<PropertyGroup Label="Globals">`
section.
- Open the solution.
- Build the solution. It correctly succeeds since we now point to the static port.
- Right click on the text "minhook.h" in the text of the include line you added. Choose to go to document. This incorrectly fails!!
- Close the solution and visual studio.
- Go to the solution folder, show hidden items, and delete the .vs folder at the top-level, This folder contains the browse info database.
- Open the solution and then show the main cpp file
- Right click on the text "minhook.h" in the text of the include line you added. Choose to go to document. This correctly succeeds



**Expected behavior**
Choosing to go to the included header file should work correctly after changing the VcpkgTriplet and reloading the project or reopening visual studio. To fix the behavior you have to delete the vc browse database. This workaround is not needed in vs2015 and vs2017, and without realizing what is happening, it leads to some very confusing/poor integration behavior.

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Unable to build a project which uses any vcpkg library due to incorrect path to vcpkg headers/libs

**Environment**
- OS: Windows
- Visual Studio 2015

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Clone vcpkg, build it
2. Install any package
3. Make integrate install
4. Run visual studio, create empty project, try to use the package (e.g. include some header)

**Expected behavior**
No errors during compilation

**Additional context**
It looks like the problem is in $(VCPKG_ROOT)\scripts\buildsystems\msbuild\vcpkg.targets.
The default $(VcpkgUserTriplet) is initialized as $(PlatformTarget)-$(VcpkgOSTarget). In solution $(PlatformTarget) seems to be empty when usertriplet is calculated. The workaround is to specify $(VcpkgPlatformTarget) variable ( the same way it is defined in vcpkg.props) and use it instead of $(PlatformTarget)

issue.title: CSV export of zone statistics from .tracy file
issue.body:
This is a proof-of-concept implementation of a simple statistics export from a .tracy file into CSV. I'm not sure if it's welcome as a part of the repository but I thought it would be useful.

The idea is to implement a command-line equivalent of the "Statistics" and "Find zone" GUI windows that will output results in a CSV format. So, you can filter a zone's name and it will spit out columns such as mean, min, max, std, etc. for each matching zone.  The `--unwrap` flag reports each zone event separately, similar to the zone list dropdown in the "Find zone" window, so you can make you own statistics. The output is printed into stdout - you can redirect it into a file or use something like [nushell](https://github.com/nushell/nushell) to process it further.

You can toggle the self time by passing the `--self` flag. Introducing similar switches to get the running or cumulative time should be simple but it would require duplicating a lot of code from TracyView.cpp which I purposefully avoided.

The code is based mostly on `tracy::View::DrawStatistics()` and `tracy::View::DrawFindZone()` and uses [cxxopts](https://github.com/jarro2783/cxxopts) to handle CLI options.
